XPEnology as an operating system for the home server (DSM 6.1.7)

February 19, 2019 Sebastian 258 comments Network , Synology DiskStation , Network , Server , Synology , XPEnology

I've already written a short story here about my server and how I use XPEnology as my operating system without a virtualization layer like ESXi or Proxmox. This post will cover how to install XPEnology directly on a computer and thus create a fully-fledged NAS.

A few basics

You probably already know what XPEnology is if you've found this post. If not, it's a port of Synology's DiskStation Manager (DSM), which runs as the operating system on all Synology NAS devices. This port makes it possible to run DSM on a regular PC. The hardware requirements are fairly low, so XPEnology will likely run on virtually any system manufactured in the last 10 years that has an Intel processor.

The problem is that you can't simply install DSM on a computer like Windows or Linux. You need a so-called bootloader, which loads the basic system during the boot process (like the boot disk used to be). DSM can then be installed on the hard drives. The bootloader is still required to boot the computer after installation. It is usually installed on a USB stick—so the motherboard used must support booting from a USB stick.

We use the DSM variant of the   Synology DiskStation DS3615xs , as it ships with an i3 processor and thus corresponds to the architecture of most computers. To prepare the USB stick, it's easiest to use a Windows computer, and that's what I'm using in this guide.

Required hardware and software

To begin the installation, we need any USB stick with 128 MB (or more) of storage and some software:

  • Create a bootable USB stick: Rufus
  • A text editor that supports Linux line breaks: Notepad++
  • The operating system: DiskStation Manager DSM 6.1.7  for the DS3615xs ( direct download )
  • The bootloader:  Jun's official v1.02b loader  as an .img file

Alternatively (and recommended)

  • jensmander's all-in-one software XPEnology Tool for Windows x64 v1.42 ( Link to the forum )

XPENOLOGY TOOL

Preliminary remarks

Why install an older version?
I'm deliberately using an older version of the bootloader and an older version of DSM. There's a simple reason for this: both are tried and tested and run extremely reliably. That's what I expect from a production system.

There are already bootloaders that support DSM 6.2, but they don't support some hardware. I've also read about problems with them several times. I don't want to take the risk, because DSM 6.1.7 can do everything I need and a lot more.

First, an important note:
We're installing DSM 6.1.7 from scratch on a PC. The bootloader used in this example doesn't allow upgrading to DSM 6.2. You'll need a different bootloader (at least version 1.03b).

The installation will proceed as follows:

  1. Read VID and PID of the USB stick
  2. Generate serial number
  3. Configure bootloader
  4. Write bootloader to the USB stick
  5. Install DSM
  6. Adjust update settings

So let's get started.

Preparing for installation

USB stick: Read VID/PID

The bootloader checks whether it's running on the correct hardware. Since everyone uses a different USB stick, we need to adjust the bootloader accordingly. So we read the VendorID and ProductID and note the values.

In XPENOLOGY TOOL, we find Portable tools the program under USB device view . We launch it and find our USB stick as Mass Storage . In my case, the values ​​look like this:

  • VID: abcd
  • PID: 1234

USB device view: Read VID and PID

Alternatively, use Windows tools:

In the Control Panel, open Device Manager and then the USB drive's properties. On the Details tab, select Device Instance Id , or Hardware-ID , from the drop-down menu and find the required values ​​there.

Generate serial number

Next, we need a serial number for the “device,” which we can generate ourselves.

In the XPENOLOGY TOOL, click Serial Generator , select our DS3615xs, and click Generate . Again, note the serial number.

XPEnology Serial Generator

Alternatively, we can also use the generator on this website use.

Download bootloader and DSM

If you haven't downloaded the required files yet, you should do so now. Either using the links above or with the XPENOLOGY TOOL, where you simply select the desired versions on the download page. The corresponding download will then open in your default browser.

XPENOLOGY TOOL Downloads

Configure bootloader

The previously determined values ​​are now entered into the bootloader. To do this, we launch OSFMount and mount partition 0 of the downloaded file DS3615xs 6.1 Jun's Mod V1.02b.img as a new drive (in my case, F: ). It's important Read-only drive to uncheck the box, as otherwise the changes we're about to make won't be saved.

OSFMount: Mount bootloader

Then we start Notepad++ , load the file F:\grub\grub.cfg and adjust the following values:

  • Line 22: 0xVID
  • Line 23: 0xPID
  • Line 24: Serial number
  • Line 25: MAC address (optional, see below)
  • Line 35: Timeout (optional, but recommended)
if serial --port=0x3F8 --speed= 115200 ; then
set has_serial=true
terminal_input --append serial
terminal_output --append serial
else
clear
fi
terminal_input --append console
terminal_output --append console
if [ x "${grub_platform}" = xefi ]; then
insmod efi_gop
insmod efi_uga
else
insmod vbe
fi
set extra_initrd= "extra.lzma"
set info= "info.txt"
set vid=0xabcd
set pid=0x1234
set sn=1130LWNxxxxxx
set mac1=68804B57BA1B
set rootdev=/dev/md0
set netif_num= 1
set extra_args_3615=''
set common_args_3615='syno_hdd_powerup_seq= 0 HddHotplug= 0 syno_hw_version=DS3615xs vender_format_version= 2 console=ttyS0,115200n8 withefi elevator=elevator quiet syno_port_thaw= 1 '
set sata_args='sata_uid= 1 sata_pcislot= 5 synoboot_satadom= 1 DiskIdxMap=0C SataPortMap= 1 SasIdxMap= 0 '
set default=' 0 '
set timeout=' 4 '
set fallback=' 1 '
if serial --port=0x3F8 --speed=115200;then set has_serial=true terminal_input --append serial terminal_output --append serial else clear fi terminal_input --append console terminal_output --append console if [ x"${grub_platform}" = xefi ]; then insmod efi_gop insmod efi_uga else insmod vbe fi set extra_initrd="extra.lzma" set info="info.txt" set vid=0xabcd set pid=0x1234 set sn=1130LWNxxxxxx set mac1=68804B57BA1B set rootdev=/dev/md0 set netif_num=1 set extra_args_3615='' set common_args_3615='syno_hdd_powerup_seq=0 HddHotplug=0 syno_hw_version=DS3615xs vender_format_version=2 console=ttyS0,115200n8 withefi elevator=elevator quiet syno_port_thaw=1' set sata_args='sata_uid=1 sata_pcislot=5 synoboot_satadom=1 DiskIdxMap=0C SataPortMap=1 SasIdxMap=0' set default='0' set timeout='4' set fallback='1'
if serial --port=0x3F8 --speed=115200;then
set has_serial=true
terminal_input --append serial
terminal_output --append serial
else
clear
fi

terminal_input --append console
terminal_output --append console

if [ x"${grub_platform}" = xefi ]; then
insmod efi_gop
insmod efi_uga
else
insmod vbe
fi

set extra_initrd="extra.lzma"
set info="info.txt"

set vid=0xabcd
set pid=0x1234
set sn=1130LWNxxxxxx
set mac1=68804B57BA1B
set rootdev=/dev/md0
set netif_num=1
set extra_args_3615=''

set common_args_3615='syno_hdd_powerup_seq=0 HddHotplug=0 syno_hw_version=DS3615xs vender_format_version=2 console=ttyS0,115200n8 withefi elevator=elevator quiet syno_port_thaw=1'

set sata_args='sata_uid=1 sata_pcislot=5 synoboot_satadom=1 DiskIdxMap=0C SataPortMap=1 SasIdxMap=0'

set default='0'
set timeout='4'
set fallback='1'

I recommend changing the MAC address to the one of the physical network card. While it also works if you leave it as is, this has one major drawback: If you install another XPEnology as a test system in VirtualBox or VMware and don't change the MAC address there either, you'll encounter network problems because MAC addresses must be unique . If you boot up the test system, your DIY NAS will most likely suddenly no longer be accessible over the network.

“Unique” is not a typo but means that one can deduce the network participant from the MAC address, and vice versa from the network participant to the MAC address.

It is also a good idea to increase the timeout of the Grub boot menu so that you have a chance to select something there.

Notepad++: customize grub.cfg

Once that's done, we save the changes, close Notepad++ and eject OSFMount the image using the button Dismount all &Exit .

Copy bootloader to USB stick

We continue with Rufus . Here we load the bootloader image we just customized and use the button to write it START to the USB stick.

Rufus: Write bootloader to USB stick

In principle, the worst is over and now remove the USB stick from the computer.

Install DSM

Time to get the NAS up and running. To do this, we plug in the USB stick and start the computer. First, we go into the BIOS and set the boot order so that the USB stick boots first. Then, we reboot, and we'll see the Grub boot menu.

Grub boot menu

By pressing the arrow keys the countdown is stopped and you can read what is written or select the desired entry.

After selecting the desired option (we take the first entry in the menu) this screen appears:

Terminal output during boot process

That was it for the terminal. Nothing more happened.

To install DSM, we now need to access our NAS's web interface. There are several ways to do this:

  • Check the router to see which IP the NAS has been assigned via DHCP and simply enter it in the web browser
  • Via the website http://find.synology.com/ let the fresh system find
  • Synology Assistant Use the

The rest is basically self-explanatory. I'll use a few images from my archive of previous posts to illustrate the next steps. To install the system, we'll, of course, use the file DSM_DS3615xs_15284.pat we downloaded earlier.

Synology Assistant: shows the virtual DiskStation as not installed

 

 

 

 

Update settings

Before you start configuring the system to your needs, you should urgently adjust the update settings. The bootloader you're using works up to and DSM 6.1.7-15284 including all security updates (currently Update 3). Accordingly, the settings should be configured so that only important updates are installed, and preferably not automatically.

DSM update settings

Please note again:
The bootloader is not compatible with DSM 6.2. A different loader must be used!

Troubleshooting

If something doesn't work, there could be many reasons for it. I've done this several times now, and when it didn't work, these were the most common causes:

  1. The wrong image was written to the stick – not the adapted one, but the original one downloaded.
  2. Error message Failed to install the file. The file is probably corrupted. (13) during DSM installation: VID or PID of the USB stick does not match the values ​​in the grub.cfg (perhaps the wrong stick was written to?).
  3. Rufus could not write the image to the flash drive: This can happen if you need to try multiple times. The drive's partitions usually have to be manually deleted before Rufus can write the image.

Personal experiences

My server has been running for several months now – and to my complete satisfaction. Initially, I had some concerns, after all, I was previously running the DS214Play. It was a bit old, but I'd never had any problems with it. No data loss, no boot issues, everything just ran smoothly. So, relying on such a DIY solution was a bit risky. What if the machine doesn't boot? What if the volumes crash and all the data is lost?

My fears proved unfounded. The system runs absolutely smoothly and flawlessly.

Even migrating the drives from the old DS214Play went great. Initially, I deleted everything I no longer needed from all the computers and hard drives I had lying around to create a backup of my 4 TB, as I didn't expect to be able to continue using the data. Ultimately, however, I didn't have enough free space, so I took the risk. I was really surprised that it worked so well.

My approach:
First, I installed a blank disk and installed DSM as described above. Then I added the other disks. The storage manager recognized the disks and marked them as faulty. After that, I just repaired the volume and installed DSM on it. This took a while, but the process was essentially self-contained.

I wrote above that the bootloader used only works up to DSM 6.1.7. Nevertheless, the security updates can be installed without any problems. Just a few days ago, I installed Update 3. It took maybe two minutes and worked even with the normal option in the boot menu.

Ultimately, I have to say that thanks to the performance of the underlying platform (i5 processor with 8GB RAM), my server is extremely versatile. In addition to all the things my DS214Play could already do, it runs the Virtual Machine Manager with two Ubuntu machines, one Debian machine, and, if necessary, Windows 10. With 8GB of RAM, you just have to be a bit careful with the memory. A RAM upgrade is definitely coming soon.

  37. Answer A user November 19, 2019

    The latest version of Active Backup for Business and all Synology apps for DSM 7.0 require this activation because Synology isn't happy about so many clones. Activation has been recognized as an option, and Synology is already testing it for 2020. DSM for the DS3615sx still has all the drivers, and each new version only includes the drivers required by the Synology hardware. One workaround: download a previous version from the Synology website, e.g., ActiveBackup-x86_64-2.1.0-0993.spk, and install it.
    Another option was mentioned in the xpenology forum: use a browser with an ad blocker that blocks the activation window. The current version will then also work in the background without activation (for now).

          • Snake 16. Mai 2020

            Huhu,

            bei mir läuft das OS ohne Stick !!!!

            Meine Vorgehensweise :
            ALLES MIT LEEREN FESTPLATTEN DURCHGEFÜHRT!!!!!

            1. OS wie oben Beschrieben Installiert

            2. After successful installation, 2nd hard drive installed (OS will be automatically mirrored on this)

            3. Remove the hard drive with the first installed OS (not the second one installed later) and put it in an external case.

            I now save myself the trouble of shutting down the system every time I had to install/remove the disks

            4. Create a partition using Windows 10's Disk Management (I'll leave the size up to you; mine is 10GB).

            5. Create another partition with the remaining hard disk capacity

            6. Install the bootloader as described above. However, you will treat the hard drive like a USB stick and only until the step where Rufus wants to install the bootloader onto the stick (hard drive).

            7. In Rufus there is now no USB stick displayed until you click on “Advanced Drive Properties”.

            8. Check “Display USB hard drives”

            9. The hard drive will now appear as a USB stick and the loader can be installed on the drive.

            10. Check in Disk Management whether the second partition (with the remaining capacity) is still there, create it again if necessary.

            11. Remove the hard drive from the external enclosure and reinsert it into the NAS.

            12. DSM starts as with the initial installation and finds your previously installed OS and will transfer the old data.

            13. Finished

          • Michael December 14, 2020

            A note about booting the DS via HDD.
            After extensive testing, I can report that there is no way to permanently install the bootloader and DSM (or even the volume) on an HDD/SSD.
            If the "boot disk" is to be used as a volume again, the bootloader partition will be overwritten, making booting from the HDD impossible.
            Of course, you can boot from the HDD, but this disk is not available for the DSM and/or volume.
            The Synology requires its own physical boot medium for the boot process.

      I have to admit I don't fully understand the question. The question here is about installing DSM on a regular computer, so I'm not selecting a NAS.
      You're probably referring to which NAS the DSM version I'm installing was originally intended for. Here, I always choose the version for the DS3615xs because that was the only one available previously, and it's always worked well. There's no underlying reason for this.

      • Answer Pharmacynix June 22, 2020

        As a layperson, I can't express myself that specifically; what I mean is this:
        in the index of /downloads/DSM/release/….., there's a dedicated download for each Synology model (hardware) (e.g., DSM_DS3018xs…).
        This gives me the impression, at least for me, that each Synology model uses a customized DSM.
        My system configuration (hardware) is identical to the DS3018xs model, except for the ECC RAM.
        Therefore, my question was whether I should use this DSM version.
        If I understand your answer correctly, it probably doesn't matter; then the same DSM would be installed everywhere?
        Best regards,
        Apotheknix

        • Answer Sebastian June 22, 2020

          For each Synology model, there is a DSM build that is tailored to the respective model's hardware.
          XPEnology is a bootloader for DSM and is suitable for x86/x64-based computers. Therefore, as far as I know, only the 3615xs, 3617xs, and 916 builds are suitable. Each of the three DSM builds has its own bootloader (XPEnology).
          In principle, it doesn't really matter which combination you use, as long as they work together. However, only the 3615xs version runs on my hardware. This, in combination with DSM 6.1.7, has been running very stable for me for a long time, which is why I always recommend this combination.
          Of course, it's up to each individual to install something else, but there are also disadvantages. Starting with DSM 6.2, for example, fewer network cards are detected. This means that the server can no longer be found on the network after DSM is installed. You just have to experiment and, if in doubt, install an additional network card.

          I have to admit, though, that I haven't followed the whole thing in a while. Product development, of course, doesn't stand still, but I simply don't have any need for updates or anything like that at the moment. Everything's working perfectly for me, so the information regarding Synology models might be a bit out of date.

    • Answer Charraeus August 4, 2020

      It's done. DSM 6.2.3 is installed and running.

      * Bootloader 1.03b DS 3615xs
      * Extract the files rd.gz and zImage from the file DSM_DS3615xs_25426.pat and write them to the second partition in synoboot.img
      * When installing in the web GUI, use the file DSM_DS3615xs_25426.pat (= DSM 6.2.3).

      Source of the finding: [https://xpenology.com/forum/topic/21663-driver-extension-jun-103b104b-for-dsm622-for-3615xs-3617xs-918/]

      2. Download the tinycore-redpill.v#.#.#.img.gz file from here:
      3. Decompress it.
      4. Burn the img file to USB.
      5. Plug the USB to the machine that is going to be used as server.
      6. Boot via USB.
      7. Open the command prompt (bottom right icon).
      8. Execude one by one the following commands:
      ./rploader.sh identifyusb now
      Y
      ./rploader.sh satamap now
      Y
      ./rploader.sh serialgen DS3615xs
      Y
      ./rploader.sh build bromolow-7.0.1-42218
      Y
      ./rploader.sh build bromolow-7.0.1-42218
      /rploader.sh backup now
      Y
      9. Reboot the device from UI (bottom left icon).
      Bootloader is now ready!
      10: Download DSM 7:
      https://global.download.synology.com/ …/DSM_DS3615xs…
      11: Boot server via USB again.

  131. Answer Roland January 20, 2022

    Hi Olli, I have a graphic showing what's possible that I'd be happy to send you. And of course the DS3615 has limitations when it comes to CPU/cores! So far everything is pretty "normal". That won't change much if you build the loader for the 3617! Which brings us to the next topic.
    What CPU does your Gen10+ have? If it's the Xeon E-2224, google it. Unfortunately, it doesn't support Intel Hyper-Threading...which is essential for the VMM. I have the Xeon E-2236 CPU installed in my Gen10+, and it works really well (performance vs. power consumption), but other CPUs, such as the Intel Core i9900, are also possible. It's always a question of budget and what you ultimately want/need to achieve.

    The Tinycore Loader is definitely the right choice, just make sure you're using the latest version 0.4.4!
    It's also important to note that you should always update after logging in.

    sudo ./rploader.sh update now

    The rest is completely fine so far, the tinycore loader is still changing quite frequently at the moment, since yesterday (I saw) the creation of the DS3617 has been fixed and seems to be running without the dpkg error.

    sudo ./rploader.sh build broadwell-7.0.1-42218

    The DS3617 loader is built using sources from the Github project (jimmyGalland).
    https://github.com/jimmyGALLAND So far so good, but if you currently (as of yesterday) want to create a loader for the DS3617, you need the correct Update2.pat file, which you can only get if you already have a working DS3617 system! Synology's Update 2 only helps to a limited extent.
    Unfortunately, this is a bit tricky, as Synology will likely take a different approach in the future, making it significantly more difficult to build the correct loader! Currently, we're only seeing this with the DS3617; the DS3615 and DS918+ are not "yet" affected.

    The correct Update 2 is 17.5 MB, making it significantly smaller than the one on Synology's website!
    All of this can be read on page 141 of the RedPill – the new loader for 6.2.4 – Discussion (Buggy25200).

    Unfortunately, the Update2 file cannot be published for legal reasons. This should be respected, and none of us knows what happened to TTG!
    Just try creating the loader for the DS3617. If you reboot after installing the DSM_DS3617xs_42218.pat and it only says "Restore" and a restore isn't possible, that's exactly the problem one of the users described yesterday, I think!

    I haven't been able to recreate it yet because I'm away on a business trip, so I've just jotted it all down here from memory... I hope it helps you a little.
    Let me know if you have any questions.
